claims.claim: Geoffrey Fryer published a 1960 warning against the proposed Nile perch introduction in the East African Agricultural Journal (vol. 25, pp. 267-270).
claims.episode_span: The fisheries scientist Geoffrey Fryer warned in 1960, in the East African Agricultural Journal, that the predator could reduce the diversity of smaller cichlids
claims.source_title: Vanishing splendor: a comprehensive review of the decline in the original fish fauna of Lake Victoria - Marine and Fishery Sciences (MAFIS)
claims.supporting_quote: Fryer G. 1960. Concerning the proposed introduction of Nile perch into Lake Victoria. East Afr Agric J. 25 (4): 267-270.

claims.claim: The first official introduction of Nile perch into Lake Victoria was made in May 1962, when 35 fish were stocked off Entebbe Pier.
claims.episode_span: the first official introductions came later, in May 1962 and September 1963 at Entebbe
claims.source_title: Observations on the biology, age, growth, maturity and sexuality of Nile perch, Lates niloticus - FAO Fisheries Report (Lake Victoria)
claims.supporting_quote: Nile perch, however, were for the first time officially introduced into Lake Victoria in May 1962 when 35 fish between 16 and 43.5 cm TL were stocked off Entebbe Pier in May 1962 amid unsettled controversy for and against it

claims.claim: Nile perch had already been surreptitiously introduced into Lake Victoria from Uganda in 1954, before the official stockings.
claims.episode_span: In August 1954 a small, unofficial release of Nile perch was made into the lake near Jinja
claims.supporting_quote: while the argument over the introduction of the Nile perch raged throughout the early 1960s, it seems that it had already been surreptitiously introduced in 1954 from Uganda.

claims.claim: A second official stocking of 339 Nile perch followed in September 1963, with the stated purpose of converting Haplochromis of little direct commercial importance into a marketable fishery.
claims.episode_span: officials therefore calculated that a single large predatory species could convert those low-value fish into a high-value, exportable product
claims.source_title: Observations on the biology, age, growth, maturity and sexuality of Nile perch, Lates niloticus - FAO Fisheries Report (Lake Victoria)
claims.supporting_quote: In September 1963 the Lake was stocked with a further 339 fish. The purpose of the introduction of Nile perch to Lake Victoria was to utilize Haplochromis which were otherwise of little direct commercial importance.

claims.claim: Lake Victoria's haplochromine cichlid flock comprised more than 500 species, almost all endemic to the lake.
claims.episode_span: the lake supported an estimated 500 species of cichlids found nowhere else
claims.supporting_quote: The main group in Lake Victoria is the haplochromine cichlids ( Haplochromis sensu lato ) with more than 500 species, almost all endemic

claims.claim: At least 200 species (about 40 percent) of Lake Victoria's haplochromine cichlids are estimated to have gone extinct after the Nile perch introduction and associated ecosystem changes.
claims.episode_span: with estimates of species lost ranging from 200 to more than 300
claims.supporting_quote: it is estimated that at least 200 species (about 40 percent) of Lake Victoria haplochromines have become extinct

claims.claim: Nile perch grow very large — up to 2 m and 200 kg — so an individual over 80 kg is well within the documented size range.
claims.episode_span: watched his workers unload a single Nile perch that weighed more than 80 kilograms
claims.supporting_quote: Nile perch can grow to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) and 200 kg (440 lb)
